clue.text: Some dry goods, guarded by three Pharisees

indicators.note: what is guarded sits protected inside its guardians, so the answer lies within the following words

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second, read across the gap

explanation.surface: Biblical Pharisees standing watch over a stock of grain or other dry provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: EPHA (or ephah) is an ancient Hebrew dry measure of about a bushel, so the lift from thrEE PHArisees fits the biblical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An epha is a Hebrew unit for measuring grain, so it denotes a quantity of dry goods.

clue.text: Bacon, perhaps poor, prepared with his help

indicators.note: food that is prepared is cut up and made into something new

blocks.note: fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: A poor slice of bacon cooked with someone's assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon is not the breakfast meat but Francis Bacon, the Elizabethan thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English thinker who shaped scientific method, an example of this profession.

clue.text: Greek character back with a woman in the temple

indicators.note: one thing in another sits within it
going back means reading the letters the wrong way

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Ena is a woman's name
mu is the twelfth Greek letter

explanation.surface: A Greek figure turns back with a woman inside the temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is used literally, though it reads as part of 'the temple'; the woman goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An athenaeum was originally a temple of Athena, and is now a name for a literary institution.

clue.text: Officer to sit with upper-class resident

blocks.note: to sit or lie is to stay put in one place
U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class
a tenant is someone resident in a property

explanation.surface: An officer is made to sit beside a posh resident, perhaps at a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a commissioned military rank, an officer below captain.

clue.text: Understatement no mature person prevaricates about

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: to prevaricate is to evade the truth, to lie
a tot is a small child, not yet grown up

explanation.surface: A grown-up downplays things, dodging the truth on some issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech of understating by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad'.

clue.text: I choose one to stop Roman Catholic prevailing

indicators.note: a stopper is pushed into an opening, so the letter is plugged inside

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
I is the Roman numeral for one
the current view is the prevailing one

explanation.surface: Someone opts to block the Catholic view that holds sway.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'I' looks like the speaker but is the definition: in physics I is the symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists use the symbol I for the flow of charge measured in amperes.

clue.text: Bird heading briefly over rescue vessel

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a title is a heading
Noah's Ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A bird heading quickly over a lifeboat at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The titlark is an old name for the meadow pipit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Isolated as Man United?

blocks.note: Al is a man's name
people united are as one

explanation.surface: Is a football club like Manchester United left out on its own?
explanation.walkthrough: Man United is the usual nickname of Manchester United football club, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone means on one's own, cut off from others, just as isolated does.

clue.text: Fish starters in the restaurant ready

indicators.note: starters come first, so the opening letters of the words are kept

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words
out means ready, as a flower is out when open

explanation.surface: The restaurant's fish starters are ready to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Where eg utensils may be purchased, get her this for mashing

definitions.text: Where eg utensils may be purchased

indicators.note: mashing crushes things into a new form, so the letters are pulped and remade

blocks.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A kitchen errand: buy her this utensil so she can mash the potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mashing' sits naturally with kitchen utensils, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The high street is a town's main shopping street, where household goods such as utensils are sold.

clue.text: Game up in Italian river, endlessly deep

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a deep voice or note is a low one

explanation.surface: A game being played up an Italian river where the water runs deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' belongs with 'Game': polo is played mounted, and up means on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team sport played on horseback, so it is a game where the players are mounted.

clue.text: Bard's work shown in text here and there

indicators.note: taking letters only here and there means skipping every other one

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and so on of these letters

explanation.surface: A piece by Shakespeare quoted at intervals in a printed text.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare, who wrote 154 poems of this form.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare, known as the Bard, wrote a famous sequence of fourteen-line poems of this kind.

clue.text: Hurt in match, leaves boxing

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a test is a Test match, an international cricket fixture
to hurt is to ache

explanation.surface: An injury sustained in a match, then the player walks out of the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves boxing' reads as quitting the sport but is the definition: something that boxes leaves, such as tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large wooden crate originally used to ship tea leaves.

clue.text: Port sacked in Ottoman push

indicators.note: a sacked city is ransacked and left in disorder

blocks.note: fodder

explanation.surface: A town plundered during an Ottoman military advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Southampton is a major port on England's south coast.

clue.text: Party member to avoid leader of Greens? There's benefit

indicators.note: to avoid something is to leave it out, so that letter is dropped
'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Greens'

blocks.note: a do is a party
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
the first letter of Greens

explanation.surface: A party member snubs the Green Party leader and gains some advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dole is unemployment pay, a state benefit handed to people out of work.

clue.text: Guinness maybe brought round, second one and last?

indicators.note: something brought round another wraps it on both sides

blocks.note: Guinness is a famous Irish dark beer of this type
a tick is a moment, a second
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone orders a Guinness round, then a second, then one last one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective but is the verb: to endure. The inserted pair goes just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick it out is to persevere to the end, to last through something hard.

clue.text: House man's inside to find reference work

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other word

blocks.note: Taurus is one of the twelve astrological houses of the zodiac
man's read as 'he is', contracted

explanation.surface: A man goes into a house to look up a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the astrological sense, a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book listing synonyms, consulted as a reference.

clue.text: Sheepish expert taken in by counterfeit notes

indicators.note: something taken in by others is held within them

blocks.note: a sham is a fake
three musical notes of the scale
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert caught out passing forged banknotes looks embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like banknotes, matching 'counterfeit', but gives the musical notes E, F and D; ACE goes between F and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced means showing embarrassment or guilt, the same as looking sheepish.

clue.text: Articles presented in trifling taste for numskull

indicators.note: things presented in something are put inside it

blocks.note: a fad is a passing, trivial craze
two articles, the definite and the indefinite

explanation.surface: Pieces served in a trifle with no taste, fit for a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifling taste' hints at a dessert, the trifle, but means a frivolous craze.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is an informal word for a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Understand everything — mostly electronic?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: dig it is slang for understand or appreciate
all is everything

explanation.surface: Can one grasp everything about electronics, more or less?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that digital is only one kind of electronic, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital technology encodes data as numbers, the basis of most modern electronic devices.

clue.text: Italian author incorporating Homer's principal nymph

indicators.note: a word incorporating another takes it into its body
the principal letter is the one at the head of the word

blocks.note: Umberto Eco wrote The Name of the Rose
the first letter of Homer

explanation.surface: An Italian novelist writing about a nymph from Homer's epics.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Echo was a mountain nymph doomed to repeat the last words of others.

clue.text: Impresario after concert books Queen

blocks.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A theatrical impresario turns up after a concert carrying books for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A promoter organises and finances concerts or shows, which is what an impresario does.

clue.text: Lives continuing as normal where cathedral burned

indicators.note: continuing means coming after, so the first piece follows on from the second

blocks.note: par is the normal standard, as in on a par
to live is to be, and he lives is he is

explanation.surface: Life goes on as usual after a cathedral fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The cathedral is Notre-Dame, badly damaged by fire in 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame cathedral in the French capital suffered a major fire in April 2019.

clue.text: Looker's twitching after surgical procedure

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming after means sitting below, so the twitch word is sent second

blocks.note: an op is an operation
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: An eye that twitches following an operation on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looker's' means belonging to the eye, matching the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic means relating to the eye or vision, the organ a person looks with.

clue.text: Award's military one churchyard elegist accepts

indicators.note: one who accepts something takes it in, so it is held within

blocks.note: Thomas Gray wrote Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
MM is the Military Medal, a British award

explanation.surface: The poet of the churchyard elegy is handed a military decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Award's' means 'Award is', the definition with a link; the Military Medal is itself an award, matching the definition's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grammy is an annual American music industry prize for recordings.

clue.text: Luxurious establishment on Piccadilly — it's a cracker

blocks.note: first meaning: the grand London hotel on Piccadilly, a street in central London
second meaning: a brand of savoury biscuit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracker' sounds like praise for a smashing hotel, but it is the American snack biscuit brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the famous London hotel and to a well-known make of salty biscuit.

clue.text: Choosing body, mischievous spirit with reader on ecstasy

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the reader word is sent second

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a lector reads lessons aloud in church
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and rash folly

explanation.surface: An impish spirit and a reader turn up together high on ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mischievous spirit' reads as an imp or elf, but here it is the Greek goddess of folly; a lector is a church reader.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is all the people entitled to vote, the body that chooses representatives.

clue.text: Art deco's altered with a line of priests

indicators.note: altered means changed, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: fodder
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An Art Deco building has been remodelled to suit a line of priests.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacerdotal is a formal adjective meaning relating to the priesthood.

clue.text: Second goal brings delight

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A second goal in a match sends the fans into raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone is informal for to thrill them, as in music that really sends you.
